names.note: Read out of doxologia.ro's line for 15 aprilie, «Sfântul Apostol Trofim».

Read out of saint.gr's line for 14 Απριλίου, «Άγιοι Αρίσταρχος, Πούδης και Τρόφιμος Απόστολοι από τους εβδομήντα», with the rank words left off; the life page heads him «Αγιος Τροφιμος Αποστολος Απο Τους Εβδομηκοντα».

His own name, read out of the Ohrid Prologue's first heading for the Julian 15 April, „Св. апостоли Аристарх, Пуд и Трофим.“, with Св. left off — it is not a rank — and апостоли left off, which is the `apostle` this folder carries in `types`. One rank word stands over three names and belongs to none of them, so what is left is the bare forename; the companionship clause this corpus keeps in his display name is not part of the source's name for him, and the heading gives no epithet and no city. `trophimus-of-antioch` already holds this same bare form, so the two fold, and the fold is recorded as deliberate in the run's findings.

Read out of the title on the name link behind the line for 15 апреля ст. ст., name page 2129, «Священномученик Трофим, апостол от 70-ти», with the rank word and the grade left off; the day's own line gives the name in the genitive, «Трофима», and the calendar's nominative has nothing fuller than the bare forename. The gate's fold key for it, 'трофим', is one this folder already holds through its Serbian form «Трофим», so the fold's membership — `trophimus-companion-of-paul`, `trophimus-companion-of-theophilus`, `trophimus-of-antioch` — is unchanged by this row, measured before and after.

source.text: Православный церковный календарь, Сретенский монастырь (days.pravoslavie.ru), 15 апреля ст. ст. — «Апп. от 70-ти Аристарха , Пуда и Трофима (ок. 67).»
source.note: The day's first entry and the only one of the five to carry a typikon icon, whose alt reads «Cовершается служба, не отмеченная в Типиконе никаким знаком» — a service the Typikon marks with no sign at all. **It keeps the three of the Seventy on the Romanian and Serbian calendars' day and not the Greek one**, which this folder's own row puts on 14 April; one row per church, so nothing was moved. The name page behind the line (2129) and the life both give «Дни памяти: 4 января (70 ап.) , 15 апреля»: the January day is the synaxis of the Seventy, a commemoration of a whole company and not a second day of his own, so no note of a second feast is written. The day prints one hymn under «Молитвы», a kontakion of the apostles in the fourth tone, which is this entry's and is added here with its English.

source.text: Calendarul zilei, Doxologia (doxologia.ro), 15 aprilie — «Sfântul Apostol Trofim»
saint.gr, το εορτολόγιο της 14ης Απριλίου — «Άγιοι Αρίσταρχος, Πούδης και Τρόφιμος Απόστολοι από τους εβδομήντα»

attestations.note: The life page heads «Τύπος εορτής: Σταθερή. Εορτάζει στις 14 Απριλίου εκάστου έτους», the same day as the listing, and gives the three no years: it places their beheading only «Στο φοβερό διωγμό του Νέρωνα (54 - 68 μ.Χ.)», in Nero's persecution, whose reign it dates 54 to 68, so no `dates` were taken. **The Greek keeps the three a day before the Romanian**, which prints them together on 15 aprilie; both pages are the same company — the three of the Seventy who were Paul's fellow workers and were beheaded with him at Rome — and the Greek adds the scriptural references it reads them out of and, for Aristarchus alone, a note that «Η μνήμη του Αγίου Αρίσταρχου επαναλαμβάνεται στις 27 Σεπτεμβρίου». The page prints two apolytikia and a kontakion, all three of them proper to the company and naming all three men; the first apolytikion and the kontakion are stored here, and the second, «Ἀπόστολοι ἅγιοι, πρεσβεύσατε τῷ ἐλεήμονι Θεῷ», is the common of apostles and was left.

source.text: Православни подсетник (pravoslavno.rs), Охридски пролог за 28.04.2026 (15. април ст. ст.) — „Св. апостоли Аристарх, Пуд и Трофим.“

attestations.note: The day's first entry, an enumerated company of three, so one row per man — the same menologion day the Romanian keeps the three on, where the Greek keeps them on 14 April; one row per church, so nothing moved. The entry puts all three among the Seventy and has them beheaded in the persecution under Nero when the apostle Paul was beheaded, and it prints no year, so nothing was added here and nothing displaced. Its one new fact about this man is that he was from Asia, with the Acts of the Apostles at chapter twenty, verse four, cited for it. This is not `trophimus-of-antioch`, the martyr under Probus whom the corpus keeps on 19 September and whose Serbian form is the same bare forename; the two are a deliberate fold recorded in the run's findings.

hymns.text: Sfinţilor Apostoli rugaţi pe Milostivul Dumnezeu, ca să dea iertare de greşeli sufletelor noastre.

source.text: doxologia.ro, «Troparul Sfinților Apostoli Aristarh, Pud, Trofim», Glasul 3

english.text: O holy apostles, entreat the merciful God to grant our souls forgiveness of sins.

hymns.text: Χορείαν τὴν τρίπλοκον, τῶν Ἀποστόλων Χριστοῦ, συμφώνως τιμήσωμεν, ὡς ποταμοὺς λογικούς, τῆς θείας χρηστότητας, Πούδην σὺν Ἀριστάρχω, καὶ Τροφίμω τῷ θείῳ λόγοις θεογνωσίας, καταρδεύσαντας κόσμον. Αὐτῶν Χριστὲ μεσιτείαις πάντας οἰκτείρησον.

source.text: saint.gr, Ἀπολυτίκιον for 14 Απριλίου under «Άγιοι Αρίσταρχος, Πούδης και Τρόφιμος Απόστολοι από τους εβδομήντα»

english.text: Let us with one voice honour the threefold choir of the apostles of Christ, as reasoning rivers of the divine goodness — Pudens with Aristarchus and with the godly Trophimus — who watered the world with the words of the knowledge of God. By their mediation, O Christ, have compassion upon us all.

hymns.text: Ὡς ἱεροί συνέκδημοι, Παύλου τοῦ θεοκήρυκος, τὴν οἰκουμένην σὺν τούτῳ διήλθετε, γνῶσιν τὴν θείαν σπείραντες, Ἀρίσταρχε θεόφρον, σὺν Τροφίμῳ τῷ Θείῳ καὶ Πούδη ἔνδοξε· διὸ καὶ ἠθληκότες, ἀξίως συνεδοξάσθητε.

source.text: saint.gr, Κοντάκιον for 14 Απριλίου under «Άγιοι Αρίσταρχος, Πούδης και Τρόφιμος Απόστολοι από τους εβδομήντα»

english.text: As holy fellow travellers of Paul the herald of God, you passed through the inhabited world with him, sowing the knowledge of God — Aristarchus of godly mind, with the divine Trophimus and Pudens the glorious. Therefore, having contended, you were worthily glorified together with him.

hymns.text: Явися апостольский честный сей праздник,/ просвещая нас и греховную мглу прогоняя, зовущим:// явися Свет, и прииде избавление.

english.text: This honoured feast of the apostles has shone forth, enlightening us and driving away the gloom of sin, as we cry out: the Light has shone forth, and deliverance has come.

source.text: Православный церковный календарь, Сретенский монастырь (days.pravoslavie.ru), 15 апреля ст. ст. — «Кондак апостолов», глас 4, under «Молитвы»
source.note: The only hymn the day prints. It is headed for the apostles and names none of the three, so it is a common of apostles serving the day's first entry, which is theirs — copied whole as the page has it, per BRIEF.md §4's ruling that a common printed under a saint's name is that saint's service. Read out of the page by `.tmp/rubody.mjs`, which reads `div.trop` under «Молитвы» and not a life page. The English is typed here.

death.note: The first years any source read for this folder gives him, and the source gives two. days.pravoslavie.ru closes the line for 15 апреля ст. ст. with «(ок. 67)», and the life it serves for the three together ends «одновременно со святым апостолом Павлом (+ ок. 67)» — at the same time as the apostle Paul, about 67. His own life page, served from the same index, closes «Святой Трофим был усечен мечом в Риме вместе с апостолами Аристархом и Пудом при императоре Нероне около 65 г.» — beheaded at Rome about 65. Both readings are the source's own, the interval holds both, and neither is chosen. The doxologia and saint.gr pages this folder already cites gave the reign, 54 to 68, and no year.
